headline: Scientists detect particles from Earth's core
standfirst: New measurements are helping us map the radioactive energy powering our planet.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Detectors worldwide are tracking geoneutrinos. These are particles made deep underground.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Researchers built a global network to capture these tiny signals from radioactive decay.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: These particles reveal the source of the heat that drives our planet's tectonic activity.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Scientists will use this data to build a clearer map of Earth's volatile interior.

caption:
Scientists are using geoneutrinos to map the interior of the Earth.

These subatomic particles are produced by the radioactive elements inside our planet. By tracking them, researchers can better understand the forces that drive tectonic movement. It is a major step forward in imaging the world beneath our feet.
